propositions: A new commit_and_push_tickets_branch entrypoint must stage and commit dirty tracker changes under an acquired write lock before delegating to push_tickets_branch, accepting optional per-command git identity parameters and strict/best-effort modes.

Rebase or merge recovery state must block commit before staging under strict mode (raising PushDeliveryError with merge-recovery-blocked reason) or warn-and-return in best-effort mode, preserving dirty content for later retry.

Lock, staging, or commit failures in strict mode raise the dependency-defined PushDeliveryError with named reasons (commit-lock-timeout, stage-failed, commit-failed); default mode logs warnings, skips push, retains uncommitted content, and allows later clean retry.

The entrypoint always delegates to push_tickets_branch after optional commit, even when the tree is clean/already-ahead; persistent rejection under strict preserves the local commit and raises PushDeliveryError instead of success.
Supplied author name/email are applied via git -c user.name/user.email without mutating global or repository config; ambient identity is used when parameters are omitted.

Direct push_tickets_branch remains completely push-only and must never stage, commit, or inspect a dirty tracker; the new commit-and-push CLI action is independent while both share the same PushDeliveryError translation boundary.
